niche: a philanthropic trust's stabilisation offers to grantees whose income is falling, scored on twelve months of income built from the grantees' quarterly portal returns and their filed annual returns, run in-house for the first time after the bureau that computed six March rounds left
answer: Strike the September 2026 Steady Ground offers at 42.55 cents per dollar of fall: 9 offers totalling $559,969 of the $560,000 pot.
answer_source: task123/submission.md, block 1 (Final Recommendation), 2026-10-09 (stage 3 write-up re-run on the rebuilt pack after hardening loop 2)

driver: A trailing four-period total at a cut-off runs only over periods whose year is closed by an annual filing on record at that cut-off, stepping back where it is not, and each period belongs to the year its own record names; a few units shortened one year to move their year end, and a calendar keyed to one year end per unit reproduces every published result, because no shortened year fell inside a published window, but at the first cut-off after the short year ends it reads that year's final period as a mid-year one, keeps those units scored on a window their own year has closed without a filing, and re-splits the fixed pool with them in it.
driver_concrete: The Steady Ground screen places each quarter in the financial year its own portal return runs within and takes a year's final quarter only from the filed annual return; three grantees moved their balance date from 30 June to 31 March in 2025-26, so their year ran nine months and March 2026 is its last quarter, with no annual return on the register at the 30 September census, so their twelve months stop at December 2025 and rule 4.1 leaves them unscored; a screen keyed to one balance date per organisation, their latest annual return's 30 June, scores them on twelve months to March 2026, offers two of them and strikes 34.11 cents on 11 names against the answer's 42.55 on nine.
stump: A competent solver rebuilds the screen as held at the 30 September census, collapses the dual-grant returns, recovers the step-back from Ledgerwood's residue rows or the twelve-month identity on the register as held, gives back all 815 published rows, every offer and every rate, reads rule 4.1 against rule 2's census list and drops the 14 grantees balancing at 31 March whose 2025-26 annual return was not on the register, and strikes the offers at 34.11 cents on 11 names, because it places every quarter on one balance date per organisation, the balance date of its latest annual return, which for the three grantees that moved from 30 June to 31 March during 2025-26 is still 30 June, so it scores them on twelve months to March 2026 and offers two of them, when each return's own year end makes March 2026 the last quarter of their nine-month year, which has no annual return on the register, so their twelve months stop at December 2025, rule 4.1 removes them, and the answer scores 132 grantees and strikes 42.55 cents on nine.

differentiation.task62: task62's tempo lineage fits a timing adjustment to a period rate from closed determinations; here nothing is fitted, the corpus fixes which trailing window a cut-off may use, ending it before any year whose annual filing was not yet on record.
differentiation.task85: task85 builds each unit's observation window from a recovered lead-time constant and a third-party start date to decide a hold; here there is no constant to recover, the window is the trailing four quarters a census may use, cut short only where the year's annual filing had not reached the register, and it re-places money in an allocation to a fixed total.

Hardening loop 1 (2026-10-09), same architecture: the decisive rung moved to rule 4.1's recency clause read against rule 2's census calendar (measured #13, validates on one population and applies to another, behind #11); the step-back is now the stop; the September pot is NZ$560,000; the ask devices are a reissued form code (D7), an absent payment channel rebuilt from the offers schedule (D4) and its pay-day clock (D8). Hardening loop 2 (2026-10-09), same architecture: the decisive rung moved to each return's own financial year against one balance date per organisation (measured #13, behind #11): three grantees moved from 30 June to 31 March in 2025-26 with a nine-month year whose annual return is not on the register, the grants register's balance-date column is gone, and rule 4.1 against rule 2 is now a lower rung (R5, the stop); K1's device moved to government co-funding paid with the Trust's operating instalments (D5), the reissued form code became a hazard (H6), and D4 and D8 hold on K2.
